files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.BackendStats
files.Summary: Stats snapshot of a backend (store or index).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.Chunk
files.Summary: A chunk produced by splitting a memory record. and are half-open offsets into the parent record's content (parentContent[StartOffset..EndOffset] == Content); the value -1 means "unset". Chunkers always set both.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.ChunkOptions
files.Summary:
Chunking parameters: structural markers, size and overlap. A trailing chunk shorter
than <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.ChunkOptions.MinChunkLength" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> merges into its predecessor (may exceed the max —
max is a packing target, min is a hard floor).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.ConsolidationOptions
files.Summary:
Tuning for one IMemoryService.ConsolidateAsync pass over a scope.

— cosine above which two records count as near-duplicates (lexical Jaccard fallback when embeddings degenerate). The OLDEST record of each duplicate group is kept, tags are unioned into it, the rest are deleted. — when on (default), records whose ExpiresAt is past are deleted first. — when on, the remaining near-duplicate clusters (similarity ≥ the ConsolidationTuning.ClusterJoinThreshold) emit one summary record each, graph-recorded when a graph extractor is wired.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.FusionOptions
files.Summary: Fusion options: RRF constant and stage weights.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.GraphOptions
files.Summary: Graph layer options: neighbor fan-out cap, walk depth, retriever behavior knobs.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IJsonlMemoryStore
files.Summary: Default JSONL-backed store contract (transactional file I/O).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IMemoryManifestCodec
files.Summary: Manifest read/write for a memory root.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IMemoryStore
files.Summary:
The durable record store seam. Every method takes the scope explicitly (kind + id) — there is no scope-less operation anywhere in the contract, so a store implementation physically cannot conflate scopes. The default JsonlMemoryStore lays out one records.jsonl per scope directory with transactional rewrites (temp file + atomic move) and tolerant reads (blank lines and legacy entries without Reps/Meta deserialize to defaults).

Concurrency contract: implementations are not required to be internally thread-safe — IMemoryService serializes store mutations per service instance; direct multi-threaded store access is the host's own synchronization problem.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IndexKind
files.Summary: The vector index backend family. — exact SIMD scan, the correctness baseline and the best choice up to tens of thousands of vectors. — deterministic k-means inverted lists; probes only nprobe clusters per query, the sweet spot for large corpora. — navigable-small-world graph, highest recall per query latency; built with immutable-index/rebuild semantics and searched with a layered greedy beam (see the architecture patent addendum). — ILGPU-kernel decoration over a CPU backend with bit-exact fallback when no device exists. All kinds pass one shared conformance suite; results are interchangeable between kinds (FlatJson included, see IVectorIndex).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryEntryModel
files.Summary:
Logical record model as persisted on disk (JSONL entry shape). <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryEntryModel.Reps" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryEntryModel.Meta" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> are optional trailing parameters: entries written before they existed
(or writers that leave them out) deserialize with null, which the store maps to the
record's empty defaults — never a null crash.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryLogFormat
files.Summary: Seriline format used by the file sink.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryLogIntegrity
files.Summary: Integrity protection applied to log entries.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryLogLevel
files.Summary: Severity of a memory log entry.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryLogSinkKind
files.Summary: Where log entries are written.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryLoggingOptions
files.Summary:
Logging configuration for the memory service. Off by default — Enabled = false means zero writes, zero log-entry allocations on the hot path, no log directory created. Enabled logging is content-minimized: log lines carry what happened (scope, operation, scores, durations), never record content itself, unless IncludeContent is explicitly set — the default-persisted posture is behavior-evidence without user-content retention.

Audit mode: Integrity = MemoryLogIntegrity.HashChain appends entries SHA-256 hash-chained to their predecessor (with monotonic sequence numbers) under a serialized gate — any modified or deleted line breaks verification, and LogChainVerifier proves integrity in one pass. RetentionDays triggers the retention sweeper; both file and console sinks are available, hosts inject their own IMemoryLogSink (SIEM, Serilog, …) through the builder.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryManifest
files.Summary: On-disk metadata describing the memory root: codecs, counts, versions.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryRecord
files.Summary:
The unit of remembered knowledge: an immutable record with identity, scope, content, and retrieval hints. Records are created by hosts and persisted through IMemoryService.RememberAsync; retrieval returns them wrapped in ScoredMemoryRecord.

Retrieval relevance is driven by (embedded and lexically indexed), boosted by and terms and exact matches in the default reranker. Optional add per-modality content (image captions, tables) that is embedded alongside the text and retrievable through the multi-representation retriever.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryRepresentation
files.Summary:
Additional per-modality content of a record: image captions, tables, audio transcripts, or any parallel content that should be retrievable alongside the record's main text. Each representation is embedded with the host's IVectorEmbedder and indexed under its own vector id (repr|<recordId>|<index>); the multi-representation retriever compares a query against every representation and keeps the best-matching one per record.

Modality contract: is a tag, not a type system — content is always string. is optional metadata for hosts that run several embedding models; the vector index namespace guard keys on the model hash + dimension, not on this field.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryRepresentationModality
files.Summary: Modality of a memory representation.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryScope
files.Summary:
One isolation boundary of memory: the (Kind, Id) pair every record, index, and log line belongs to. Records written to one scope are structurally invisible to operations on another — the storage root layout pins each scope to its own directory tree and the index registry keys indexes by the exact scope pair.

Scopes may carry a chain for hierarchical fan-out (query plans target a root and resolve child scopes), but lookups never fall through to parents: a query against scope A sees scope A, nothing else, whatever its ancestry.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryScopeKind
files.Summary: The isolation axis of a . One record lives in exactly one (Kind, Id) pair; the kind determines what the id conventionally names: Platform (one surface — e.g. per chat platform), Session (one conversation or run), Tenant (one customer — multi-tenant hosts), Purpose (one knowledge base or domain), Custom (host-defined). Kinds map to storage path segments, so cross-kind and cross-id isolation are identical by construction. Unknown on-disk kinds degrade to Custom on read.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryServiceOptions
files.Summary:
The root options record for MemoryService: the host's per-domain tuning, injected once at build time. Each section covers one pipeline concern — (root layout), (backend + dim), (walk tuning), (RRF weights), (dedup/cluster thresholds),

Section records carry safe defaults; a host that passes all defaults gets the reference pipeline. Optional capabilities (grader, graph extractor, reranker, log sink) are injected via MemoryServiceBuilder rather than this record — options tune behavior, wiring enables capabilities.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.QueryPlan
files.Summary: Declarative retrieval plan: an ordered set of steps the runner executes.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.QueryPlanStep
files.Summary: One step of a declarative plan (fan-out namespaces, merge, iterate).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.QueryTokens
files.Summary:
Pure query-text token helpers shared by text-processing packages (keyword rewriting,
score-boost reranking). Stateless lookups and a compiled regex only; this class is the
architecture-sanctioned pure-function static: no I/O, no ambient state, deterministic.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.RetrievalFilters
files.Summary: Immutable tag/category/date filter set for retrieval.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.RetrievalProvenance
files.Summary: Provenance of a scored memory record: which retriever produced it and per-stage scores.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.RetrievalQuery
files.Summary:
A scope-bound retrieval request: what to look for, where to look, and how much to return. Passed to IMemoryService.RecallAsync.

is authoritative — results are drawn from that scope's indexes only, never from other scopes. runs through the full pipeline (embedding + BM25 lexical + fusion + optional rerank/corrective loop); an empty or whitespace text short-circuits to an empty result. bounds the returned records. (tags, category, date-from) are applied after fusion, so they never affect ranking of the candidates they admit. (when set) executes a declarative multi-scope fan-out instead of a single-scope lookup — see QueryPlanRunner.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.RetrievalResult
files.Summary:
The outcome of IMemoryService.RecallAsync: the scored records, best first, plus per-stage diagnostics.

is ordered by descending with deterministic tie-breaks by record id. carries one entry per pipeline stage (dense, lexical, fusion, rerank, corrective retries) with durations and stage-specific metrics — feed it to the eval harness for Recall@k/MRR/NDCG.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.RetrievalStageDiagnostics
files.Summary: Diagnostics of one retrieval stage (scores and timing).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.ScoredId
files.Summary: A scored hit from a store/index search: scope kind, scope id, id, score.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.ScoredMemoryRecord
files.Summary:
A record matched by a retrieval, its relevance score, and where the score came from.
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.ScoredMemoryRecord.Provenance" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> names the stage that produced the score and carries per-stage
subscores (e.g. the fused RRF score plus the rerank-adjusted score), so ranking changes
across pipeline stages remain explainable end to end.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.StorageOptions
files.Summary: FlatJson store options: root folder + durability settings.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.VectorOptions
files.Summary: Vector index options: backend kind, model hash, dimension, default top-k.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Chunking.ChunkIdCodec
files.Summary: Canonical chunk-id codec: "scopeKind|scopeId|recordId|chunkIndex" (ordinal pipe-separated). Embeds the parent's scope so a chunk id alone is enough to locate its parent record in the store, and keeps record ids from colliding across scopes.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Chunking.ChunkIdParts
files.Summary: The four components of a canonical chunk id.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Chunking.ChunkParentResolver
files.Summary:
Resolves a canonical chunk id to its parent record via an <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IMemoryStore" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
snapshot of the scope embedded in the id. A malformed id or a missing parent record
yields null; the chunk index itself is never validated against a live chunk list.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Chunking.IChunker
files.Summary:
Splits a record's content into embedded units for the dense index. Chunks carry exact offsets back into the original content, so a chunk hit resolves to its parent record — the whole record is always what surfaces in results, never the fragment.

Implementations: StructuredChunker cuts on markdown structure first (headings, paragraphs, then sentences) and only hard-slices oversized content; SizeChunker packs by size with optional overlap — fixed-stride windows in geometry mode, shared whole words in separator mode. Both preserve every character of content across the split (mod whitespace at cut points).

Chunk ids are scope-qualified (kind|scope-id|record-id|index) — see ChunkIdCodec; ids containing the '|' separator are rejected at compose time.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Chunking.IParentResolver
files.Summary: Resolves chunk ids back to their parent record (parent-document recall).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Chunking.SizeChunker
files.Summary: Pure size + overlap splitting for unstructured content. Two modes: geometry (no separator): with = 0 content is cut at separators (paragraph break → newline → sentence terminator → hard slice of exactly max) with separator whitespace consumed at cuts; with overlap > 0 fixed stride windows (stride = max − overlap, window = max) guarantee consecutive chunks share exactly Overlap characters and no character is lost. Separator mode: words are packed and joined by the separator; Overlap counts shared whole words repeated from the previous chunk's tail (rolling window), so shared text matches word for word.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Chunking.StructuredChunker
files.Summary:
Splits record content by markdown structure: headings become their own chunks, each
paragraph is a chunk (or sentence-packed pieces when oversized; a single over-max
sentence hard-slices). Non-structural mode (<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.ChunkOptions.RespectStructure" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
= false) delegates to <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Chunking.SizeChunker" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. Overlap is only applied by
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Chunking.SizeChunker" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>; structural chunking keeps paragraphs intact. All content is
preserved verbatim (modulo whitespace between structural cuts) with exact offsets.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.ClusterSummarizer
files.Summary:
Builds a summary <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryRecord" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> from a near-duplicate cluster: the
concatenated member keys plus deterministic representative excerpts, category
"summary", and Meta carrying the cluster-summary flag, member count, cluster id and
member ids. Cluster id = sha256 over ordinal member ids, so the same cluster always
maps to the same summary id (idempotent re-consolidation).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.ConsolidationReport
files.Summary: Outcome counters of one consolidation pass over a scope.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.ConsolidationReportMeta
files.Summary:
Side channel that attaches the pass <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.ConsolidationReport" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> to the records
returned by <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.IMemoryConsolidator" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: the interface signature is fixed by the
scaffold, so the report travels as a "consolidation-report" Meta entry on each returned
record (returned copies only — store contents are never touched by this). Pure
helpers over immutable records; the serializer options are immutable after creation.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.ConsolidationTuning
files.Summary:
Consolidation pass tuning knobs, layered over <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.ConsolidationOptions" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
(thresholds have defaults and stay host-overridable via the base record).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.IClusterSummarizer
files.Summary: Summarizes a cluster of records into a new summary record.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.IDedupDetector
files.Summary: Near-duplicate detection via similarity threshold.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.IMemoryConsolidator
files.Summary: Consolidation pass over a scope: dedup, merge, TTL expiry, cluster summaries.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.MemoryConsolidator
files.Summary:
One consolidation pass over a scope, executed against the scope-bound
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IMemoryStore" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: (1) TTL expiry deletes records whose ExpiresAt is in the
past, (2) near-duplicate detection via <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.IDedupDetector" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> keeps the oldest
record of each duplicate group and unions the tags of the removed duplicates into the
kept record, (3) remaining records are clustered by embedding similarity and clusters
of sufficient size are emitted as summary records via <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.IClusterSummarizer" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>,
(4) all mutations are counted in a <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.ConsolidationReport" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> attached to the
returned records. Survivors and summaries are returned (survivors first, summaries
last); an empty scope is a no-op returning an empty list. Every deletion goes through
the store's scope-bound API — cross-scope access stays structurally impossible.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.ThresholdDedupDetector
files.Summary:
Near-duplicate detection: cosine over records embedded via the injected
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorEmbedder" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>, falling back to lexical Jaccard over token sets when
both vectors degenerate (zero norm). A pair counts as duplicate when its similarity
is greater than or equal to the given threshold. Arguments are ordered
deterministically (earlier-id first) before evaluation, so the result never depends
on call-site order; evaluation itself is pure. This type holds no mutable state.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.CorrectionOptions
files.Summary:
Options for the corrective retrieval pipeline. Typed options injected by the host
(no environment configuration in product code).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.CorrectiveRetriever.StageNames
files.Summary: Diagnostic stage names reported in <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.RetrievalStageDiagnostics.Stage" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.CorrectiveRetriever
files.Summary:
Grader-gated corrective retrieval around an injected <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.IHybridRetriever" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>:
candidates pass or are dropped per <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Correction.IRetrievalGrader" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>; below-floor
candidates are not yielded. One rewrite-and-retry cycle via <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Correction.IQueryRewriter" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
runs when the first pass graded any candidate <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Correction.RetrievalGrade.Uncertain" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> or
yielded nothing acceptable (all-Irrelevant/all-below-floor). When nothing survives, the
optional <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Correction.IExternalFetcher" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> hook (null = skip) runs once. Every stage
reports diagnostics.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.GradedCandidate
files.Summary: A grade assigned to one candidate.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.IExternalFetcher
files.Summary:
Fetches content from external sources (host-injected; the library stays network-agnostic).
Returning an empty list (or null) yields no fetched-stage content.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.IQueryRewriter
files.Summary: Rewrites/expands a query for corrective retrieval (host-injected when an LLM-backed rewriter is desired).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.IRetrievalGrader
files.Summary: Grades candidates for relevance (host-injected).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.KeywordQueryRewriter
files.Summary:
Deterministic, zero-dependency query rewriter: distills the query to its key terms via
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.QueryTokens.KeyTerms(System.String)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> — stopwords stripped (acronyms preserved),
duplicates collapsed. Emits a single-space-joined term list; empty queries rewrite to
the empty string.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Correction.RetrievalGrade
files.Summary: Grade of a retrieved candidate.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.DefaultEvalServiceFactory
files.Summary:
Default eval wiring: a real <xref href="ProvostXMemory.MemoryService" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> over the transactional JSONL
store + own-engine flat index + RRF, powered by the deterministic
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Eval.ClusterHashEmbedder" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (no real model anywhere). Any host can substitute its
own <xref href="ProvostXMemory.EvalServiceFactory" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> to eval its production wiring instead.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.ClusterHashEmbedder
files.Summary:
Deterministic fake embedder for eval runs — NOT a real model. Cluster-preserving:
every token maps to a fixed slot from a stable FNV-1a hash; each of a record's tokens
adds a fixed cluster id + token hash signature so similar content (shared cluster
terms) lands near the same direction, with per-record seeded noise amplitude only.
No randomness at embed time: same text → same vector, always.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.DeterministicEvalCorpus
files.Summary:
Seeded synthetic corpus: N records per scope across M scopes, round-robin assigned to
keyword clusters (exact balance) so every scope/cluster pair yields the same number of
expected matches per query. Content
is a seeded shuffle of the record's cluster terms plus filler words, one hard-negative
term from a seeded foreign cluster, and one seeded noise token — derivable relevance
without an LLM: the expected matches for a cluster query are exactly that cluster's
records. Identical seeds yield byte-identical corpora, verified via <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Eval.DeterministicEvalCorpus.DeterminismHash" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalCase
files.Summary:
One golden retrieval case: a query bound to a scope plus the record ids a good
retriever should surface. Relevance is binary (1.0) unless graded weights are given.
The query's TopK is overridden by the eval runner options' TopK at run time.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalCaseMetrics
files.Summary:
Metrics for one eval case: Recall@k, Precision@k, MRR and NDCG@k over the ranked
    result ids judged against the case's golden relevance.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalCaseSet
files.Summary:
A named set of golden eval cases grouped under one logical set id. Case ids must be
unique within a scope (cross-scope ids may repeat); the set is immutable after creation.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalCaseTrace
files.Summary:
Per-case ranked outcome: returned ids with their graded relevance gains and
    how many returned records came from a scope other than the case's own (isolation guard).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalCaseTraceHit
files.Summary: One returned id with its graded relevance gain for this case.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalMetricBreakdownEntry
files.Summary: Metric means for a breakdown group (scope or retriever stage).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalMetricMath
files.Summary:
The metric formulas, implemented independently of any search engine and unit-tested against hand-computed values:
  • Recall@k = |relevant ∩ top-k| / |relevant| (0 when no relevant ids).
  • Precision@k = |relevant ∩ top-k| / k (unfilled top-k counts against precision).
  • MRR = 1 / rank of the first relevant hit, else 0.
  • NDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k with DCG = Σ relᵢ / log₂(rank + 1), rank starting at 1.
All instance methods (no static state shared across instances).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalMetricThresholds
files.Summary:
Minimum metric values for the aggregate <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalReport" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. A violation is any
actual value strictly below its threshold. All thresholds optional (null = unchecked).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalMetrics
files.Summary: Aggregate over all cases: plain means of the per-case metric values.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalReport
files.Summary:
Serializable result of running an <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalCaseSet" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: per-case metrics, the
aggregate, per-scope and per-stage breakdowns, threshold violations, and the per-case
ranked id lists (with graded gains) for diffing. JSON-ready via System.Text.Json.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalReportJson
files.Summary: JSON (de)serialization for <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalReport" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (System.Text.Json).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.MemoryScopeComparer
files.Summary: Ordinal scope comparison helper (Kind + Id); shared by eval components.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.MetricThresholdViolation
files.Summary: One threshold violation: metric name, actual vs required.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Eval.MetricThresholdViolations
files.Summary: Immutable violation list; empty when all thresholds pass.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.EvalRunner
files.Summary:
Runs an <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalCaseSet" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> against a freshly built service from an
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.EvalServiceFactory" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: materializes the corpus records under a fresh temp
root, builds indexes per scope, replays every golden query, computes all metrics and
breakdowns, checks thresholds, and produces a JSON-serializable <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Eval.EvalReport" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.
The runner never constructs a service itself — hosts control wiring via the factory.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.EvalRunnerOptions
files.Summary: Per-run knobs for <xref href="ProvostXMemory.EvalRunner" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.EvalServiceFactory
files.Summary:
Host-pluggable service construction for eval runs: given a fresh root path the host
builds an <xref href="ProvostXMemory.IMemoryService" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> exactly as it does in production.
Implementations must return a service with no records yet — the runner owns corpus
loadout and index building.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex01_Quickstart
files.Summary:
Minimal end-to-end flow (the README quickstart, made runnable): build a service,
remember five facts, build indexes, recall, and print the ranked hits.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex02_Scopes
files.Summary:
Multi-tenant isolation: the SAME record key is written into three tenant scopes with
different content; recall in each scope only ever sees that scope's own record, and
lookups from a foreign scope find nothing.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex03_HybridSearch
files.Summary:
Hybrid retrieval (BM25-style lexical + dense vector, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion):
a keyword-only hit and a semantic-only hit answer different halves of the corpus —
the fused query surfaces both.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex04_Backends
files.Summary:
Backend parity: the same dataset is loaded into four services — engine Flat, IVF,
HNSW, and the zero-dependency FlatJson index — plus the GPU backend (with a fallback
note: without a GPU the factory transparently runs its CPU kernels). Every backend
returns the same hits; timings are printed per backend.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex05_Consolidation
files.Summary:
Consolidation: near-duplicate records are merged into one survivor plus a cluster
summary record; TTL-expired records are deleted. Before/after counts and the summary
record are printed.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex06_GraphRetrieval
files.Summary:
Graph retrieval: records mentioning shared entities form an entity/relation graph at
index time (heuristic extractor). A graph-connected recall through the entity subgraph
surfaces ALL records touching an entity — including records the plain lexical/dense
query would miss because they share no query token.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex07_CorrectiveLoop
files.Summary:
Corrective recall: a weak first-pass query is graded, rewritten, and retried. The
deterministic fake grader accepts only strong fused hits (both retrieval stages
contribute); the built-in keyword rewriter distills the noisy query so the retry pass
ranks the target record on top. Diagnostics prove the rewrite-and-retry cycle ran.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex08_LoggingAudit
files.Summary:
Audit logging with hash-chain integrity: file logging is enabled, service operations
append chained entries, <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Logging.LogChainVerifier" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> validates the chain — and after
one line is tampered with, the verifier pinpoints the broken line.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex09_EvalHarness
files.Summary:
Eval harness: the deterministic seeded corpus is loaded into a fresh service, every
golden query is replayed, and a Recall@k / MRR / NDCG report is printed. Identical
seeds produce byte-identical corpora and runs.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.Ex10_RestartPersistence
files.Summary:
Restart persistence: records written through the service survive disposal — a brand
new service instance rebuilt over the same root recalls them, proving the transactional
JSONL store is the durable source of truth (indexes are rebuilt from it).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Examples.ExampleBase

FlatJson factory: one <xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorNamespaceFile" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> per created scope index,

Shared wiring helper for the examples: every service is composed exactly as a host

Entry point for the runnable example set. With no arguments every example runs in

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Fusion.IResultFuser
files.Summary: Fuses multiple ranked lists (RRF, k=60 default, weighted, deterministic ties).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Fusion.RankedList
files.Summary: A single ranked list input to fusion: source name plus ranked hits.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Fusion.ReciprocalRankFuser
files.Summary:
Reciprocal Rank Fusion: each item scores sum over lists of weight / (k + rank),
rank starting at 1. Default k = 60. Stage sources ("dense", "lexical") use the
stage weights from <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.FusionOptions" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>; unknown sources weigh 1.0. Ties break
deterministically by id (ordinal) then by best (lowest) rank across lists.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.ExtractionResult
files.Summary: Entity + relation extraction result.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.GraphCluster
files.Summary: A graph cluster (community) with an optional summary record id.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.GraphEntity
ProvostXMemory.Graph.GraphRelation
files.Summary:
A relation between two graph entities, treated as undirected for traversal.
Weight is implicit: <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.GraphRelation.RecordIds" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.Count equals the number of supporting records.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.GraphRetriever
files.Summary:
Graph-backed retriever: lowercased query tokens are matched against entity ids and
entity names/aliases (via <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.IMemoryGraphStore.SearchEntitiesAsync(System.String%2cSystem.Int32%2cSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>) and against
record tags from the scope's snapshot; matched entities seed a multi-source neighbor walk up
to <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.GraphOptions.MaxHops" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> hops via <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.IMemoryGraphStore.NeighborsAsync(System.String%2cSystem.Int32%2cSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>;
records touched by discovered entities and their relations plus
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.GraphCluster.SummaryRecordId" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> of matched clusters are scored by hop distance
(direct evidence = 1.0, each additional hop × 0.5 decay; independent evidence sums).
Entity/relation extraction is an index-time concern (<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.IEntityExtractor" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>);
this retriever is deliberately query-time token-based.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.HeuristicEntityExtractor
files.Summary:
Zero-dependency heuristic extractor: capitalized multi-word phrases and keyword/tag
matches become entities; entities co-occurring inside one record become relations
(label "co-occurs", weight = number of supporting records). Deliberately simple
default; hosts inject stronger <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.IEntityExtractor" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> implementations.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.IEntityExtractor
files.Summary: Host-injected entity/relation extractor (LLM or heuristic).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.IGraphRetriever
files.Summary: Retrieves records from a relevant subgraph plus cluster summaries.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.IMemoryGraphStore
files.Summary: Graph-backed store over memory records: entities, relations, paths, clusters.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.IMemoryGraphStoreResolver
files.Summary:
Resolves the scope-pinned graph store for a memory scope. Implementations must
guarantee that the returned store is bound to exactly the requested scope, so
cross-scope access stays structurally impossible.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Graph.JsonlMemoryGraphStore
files.Summary: JSONL-backed graph store: graph/entities.jsonl, graph/relations.jsonl and graph/clusters.jsonl per scope directory (via ). Paths resolve only through the layout, so cross-scope access stays structurally impossible. Every mutation rewrites the affected JSONL file transactionally via .

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.GraphIndexLedger
files.Summary:
Index-time graph maintenance over the scope-pinned <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.IMemoryGraphStore" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
(resolved via <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.IMemoryGraphStoreResolver" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>): per record, the wired
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Graph.IEntityExtractor" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>'s entities/relations are upserted for the record's
scope only; when a record is forgotten, its mentions are dropped by re-extracting
the scope's remaining snapshot. The ledger itself holds no per-record entity cache —
graph stores accumulate weight by design, so Forget rebuilds the affected entity
mention lists from the surviving records. Scope comes from the record; the resolver
is scope-exact by contract.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.IMemoryService
files.Summary:
The single public surface of the ProvostXMemory library. Host applications see this interface — plus the options records they pass to — and nothing else. Every capability of the library (durable storage, hybrid lexical and dense-vector retrieval, fusion, reranking, optional corrective and graph retrieval, consolidation, and audit-grade logging) is reachable through the members below.

Scope isolation. Every record belongs to exactly one (platform, session, tenant, purpose, or custom). Every operation is scope-bound; a record written to scope A is structurally invisible to operations on scope B — the storage layout and the index registry make cross-scope access impossible rather than merely discouraged.

Concurrency. Implementations are safe for concurrent use from multiple threads. Mutations (Remember/Update/Forget) are serialized per service instance; embedding computation happens outside the serialization gate, so concurrent callers do not block on model latency.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.IScopesAware
files.Summary: Implemented by stores that can enumerate their scopes natively.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.Bm25Scorer
files.Summary:
BM25-lite scoring: saturated term frequency (k1 = 1.2) × IDF plus a key-match boost
(default 2.0) on key-term hits and a modest single-term category match bonus (0.5).
Classic BM25-lite: no length normalization, no third-party dependencies. Stateless
pure scoring — corpus statistics are passed in per call (the index owns them).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.CorpusStatistics
files.Summary: Immutable corpus-level statistics: document count plus per-term stats.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.IBm25Scorer
files.Summary:
BM25-lite scoring: saturated term frequency (k1 = 1.2) × IDF, plus a key-match boost
on key-term hits and a single-term category match bonus. Corpus statistics are passed
per call (owned by the index, which keeps them current after build/add).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.ILexicalIndex
files.Summary:
The lexical half of hybrid retrieval: a BM25-weighted inverted index over record text, kept in sync by the memory service (records remember/update → IncrementalAdd; forget → Remove). Complements the dense stage by matching exact terms embeddings miss (identifiers, acronyms, version numbers); both stages fuse into one ranking via IResultFuser.

Contract: tokens are lowercase alphanumeric words (no stemming, no external NLP); scores are saturated-TF × IDF with a key-match boost. The index itself is not thread-safe — the memory service serializes all mutations; external callers must not share an instance unsynchronized.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.LexicalDocument
files.Summary: A tokenized document with optional key terms and category.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.LexicalIndex
files.Summary:
BM25-lite keyword index over documents. Inverted postings over body terms, plus
key-term and exact-category maps so key-only and category-only matches surface.
Scoring is delegated to <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Lexical.IBm25Scorer" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>; ordering is fully deterministic
(score desc, then document id ascending).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.LexicalPosting
files.Summary: One body posting: (document id, term frequency).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.LexicalTermCounts
files.Summary:
Term-frequency / token-set helpers over pre-tokenized term lists.
Pure functions over their inputs; intentionally static per architecture rule.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.LexicalTokenizer
files.Summary:
Lowercases text and extracts contiguous [a0-9] word tokens (letters, digits, underscore).
Pure helpers (stateless string transforms); intentionally static per architecture rule.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.ScoredLexicalId
files.Summary: Lexical index search hit: id plus BM25-lite score.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Lexical.TermStat
files.Summary: Immutable per-term corpus statistics for BM25 scoring.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.ConsoleMemoryLogSink
files.Summary: Writes log entries to standard output as plain text lines.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.FileMemoryLogSink
files.Summary: Append-only file sink with per-date rolling and lazy directory creation. Each line is written with FileShare.Read and flushed immediately.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.HashChainAppender
files.Summary:
Computes SHA-256 entry hashes chained to the previous entry's hash and
assigns monotonic sequence numbers. Pure computation is static; the
instance tracks only the chain head.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.IMemoryLogSink
files.Summary: Destination for memory log entries.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.LogChainVerificationResult
files.Summary: Result of verifying a hash-chained log file.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.LogChainVerifier
files.Summary:
Pure verifier for hash-chained JSON-lines log files. Reads a file, checks
hash-chain linkage and sequence-number continuity, and reports the first
broken line when the log has been tampered with.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.MemoryLogCategory
files.Summary: Functional area a memory log entry belongs to.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.MemoryLogEntry
files.Summary: A single memory log entry.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.MemoryLogJson
files.Summary: JSON (de)serialization helpers for log lines.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.MemoryLogJsonLine
files.Summary: Wire shape of a log entry line used by the file sink and the chain verifier.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.MemoryLogScope
files.Summary: Scope information attached to a log entry.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.MemoryLogger
files.Summary:
Facade over the logging pipeline: on/off gate, level filter, hash chaining
and fan-out to the configured sink. When disabled, no entry objects are
allocated and no writes occur.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Logging.RetentionSweeper
files.Summary: Deletes log files older than the configured retention window.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.MemoryService
files.Summary:
Composition root: takes <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryServiceOptions" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> plus injected dependencies
and owns the configured retrieval pipeline. Remember/Forget/Update maintain the
per-scope indexes alongside the store; Recall routes through hybrid → optional
corrective → plan (when the query carries one) → optional rerank. Every store access
goes through the scope-bound <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IMemoryStore" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> API, so cross-scope isolation
is structural. Per-scope indexes are created lazily and registered scope-exact.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.MemoryServiceBuilder
files.Summary:
Fluent wiring helper for <xref href="ProvostXMemory.MemoryService" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. Collects the host's choices and
hands them to the <xref href="ProvostXMemory.MemoryService" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> constructor — still plain constructor
injection underneath, no service locator, no ambient container.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.MemoryServicePipelineOptions
files.Summary:
Pipeline wiring knobs layered over <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryServiceOptions" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: which extra
retrieval stages run during Recall/Remember and maintenance bounds for index updates.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Reranking.ClientBackedReranker
files.Summary:
Adapter wrapping the host-injected <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Reranking.IRerankerClient" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: the client returns
best-first ids; this adapter maps ids back to candidates, keeps provenance of the
wrapped (fused) scores, and handles unlisted candidates per
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Reranking.ClientBackedRerankerOptions" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. The client itself stays host-owned infrastructure.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Reranking.ClientBackedRerankerOptions
files.Summary:
Options for <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Reranking.ClientBackedReranker" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: which client ids to trust and where
fallback keeps unlisted/dropped candidates.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Reranking.IReranker
files.Summary:
The post-fusion scoring stage: reranks fused candidates against the query. The default ScoreBoostReranker adds deterministic boosts (tag/key/category term matches) and penalties (extremely short or long content) without ever dropping a candidate; a NoopReranker preserves fused order. Hosts may inject an LLM- or cross-encoder-backed reranker through this interface — the library stays model-free.

Ranks exactly once: the retrieval pipeline reranks internally; a second pass over already-reranked results compounds boosts (found by audit) — hosts calling directly own that responsibility.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Reranking.IRerankerClient
files.Summary:
Optional external rerank service contract (LLM/cross-encoder API, host-injected).
The library never constructs a client; hosts adapt their transport into this contract.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Reranking.NoopReranker
files.Summary: Identity reranker: returns candidates unchanged (deterministic pass-through).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Reranking.ScoreBoostReranker
files.Summary:
Deterministic, zero-dependency reranker: additive boosts for tag/key/category matches
against the query's key terms, additive penalties for extremely short or long content.
Ties break by original rank (stable from the fused order); the output preserves input
casing of scores and never drops candidates.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Reranking.ScoreBoostRerankerOptions
files.Summary: Options for <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Reranking.ScoreBoostReranker" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. Deterministic, zero-dependency tuning.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.HybridRetriever
files.Summary:
Hybrid retrieval within one scope: dense (vector index) and lexical (BM25-lite index)
searches run concurrently over the scope's registered artifacts, are fused via the
injected <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Fusion.IResultFuser" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (RRF over "dense"/"lexical" rank lists), resolved
against the scope's records, and optionally reranked by an injected <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Reranking.IReranker" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.
Scope comes from the query and all registry lookups are scope-exact.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.ICorrectiveRetriever
files.Summary: Grader-gated hybrid retrieval with rewrite loop (corrective).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.IHybridRetriever
files.Summary: Dense + lexical retrieval in parallel → fused results.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.IMultiRepresentationRetriever
files.Summary: Query across modalities (multi-representation records).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.IQueryPlanRunner
files.Summary: Executes a declarative <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.QueryPlan" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (fan-out namespaces, merge, iterate).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.IQueryTextRewriter
files.Summary:
Rewrites a query's plain text before a second retrieval pass (host-injected;
typically an LLM-backed rewriter, a lexical distiller, or a spell corrector).
Lives in Retrieval (not Correction) so plan fan-out can iterate without the
Correction package as a dependency.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.IScopeIndexRegistry
files.Summary:
Maps a <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryScope" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> to its per-scope retrieval artifacts. Implementations
must be scope-exact: a lookup for scope A never returns an artifact of scope B
(no parent fallthrough, no default forwarding) — cross-scope access stays
structurally impossible.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.InMemoryScopeIndexRegistry
files.Summary:
In-memory scope → artifact registry for single-process hosts and test harnesses.
Keys are the exact (Kind, Id) pair; lookups never fall through to parent or child scopes.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.KeywordQueryTextRewriter
files.Summary:
Zero-dependency <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.IQueryTextRewriter" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>: distills the query text to its
key terms via <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.QueryTokens.KeyTerms(System.String)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> — stopwords stripped (acronyms
preserved), duplicates collapsed, first-appearance order. Empty queries stay empty.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.MultiRepresentationRetriever
files.Summary: Multi-representation retrieval: instead of scoring whole-record content, the query is embedded once and compared against each representation's precomputed vector for the requested modality. Representation vectors are indexed in the vector index under "repr|<recordId>|<index>" ids (see ); hits map back to their parent record, per-record scores take the best-matching representation, and per-modality provenance is attached. Scope comes from the query; registry lookups are scope-exact.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.QueryPlanRunner.IScopeResolver
files.Summary: Resolves target scope strings ("Kind/Id") against a root scope.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.QueryPlanRunner.QueryPlanRunnerOptions
files.Summary: Tuning for the plan runner: weak-evidence thresholds and pass behavior.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.QueryPlanRunner
files.Summary: Executes a declarative . Each step fans out to its target scopes (target scope strings are "<scope-kind>/<scope-id>" pairs; empty targets mean the query's own scope), runs the injected retriever in every target scope with per-scope ids namespaced, and merges the step lists via the injected . When every step's top score is below , a single second pass runs once against the rewritten text from the injected ; its results replace the first pass. Record resolution happens against each target scope's own snapshot — a record id from scope A never resolves into scope B.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.RetrievalFilterApplier
files.Summary:
Pure predicate that enforces the <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.RetrievalFilters" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> carried on a
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.RetrievalQuery" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> against resolved records: category exact-match,
tag any-match, and date window (From/To) on the record's <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryRecord.CreatedAt" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>.
A null filter set matches everything, so unfiltered retrieval is behaviorally unchanged.
Intentionally static: it is a pure function per the architecture rule.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.RootChildScopeResolver
files.Summary: Default plan-fan-out scope resolution: a target string names either the root scope itself ("<Kind>/<Id>", case-insensitive) or a child scope built via ("<ChildKind>/<ChildId>" over the root). Resolving a child pins the parent, so fan-out targets are always descendants or the root itself — never unrelated scopes.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Storage.AtomicFileWriter.WriteResult
files.Summary: Result of an atomic write: the destination path and the bytes written.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Storage.AtomicFileWriter
files.Summary:
Durability primitive for the storage layer: writes payload to a temporary
file in the destination directory, fsyncs it, then atomically moves it over
the destination. Temp leftovers from crashed writers are cleaned up on the
next write to the same directory.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Storage.JsonlMemoryStore
files.Summary: Default JSONL-backed store: one append/rewrite-friendly records.jsonl per scope, one JSON document per line, transactional rewrite on every mutation. All operations take the scope as a required parameter and resolve paths only through , so cross-scope access is structurally impossible.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Storage.MemoryManifestCodec
files.Summary: Manifest read/write for a memory root (JSON, atomic swap); missing file reads as empty.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Storage.MemoryRootLayout
files.Summary: Root folder + scope path resolution: <root>/<scope-kind>/<scope-id>/.... Every caller-supplied segment is validated to be a single, safe path segment (no traversal, no separators, no Windows-reserved names) and every resolved path is checked to stay inside the root folder.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Telemetry.IMemoryTelemetry
files.Summary: Query/consolidation timings, per-stage scores, backend stats (host-injected sink; default no-op).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Telemetry.InMemoryMemoryTelemetry
files.Summary:
Capture-style telemetry sink that records reported stages and backend stats in
memory. Intended for tests and lightweight in-process diagnostics; not durable.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.Telemetry.NoopMemoryTelemetry
files.Summary: Zero-op default telemetry sink. Never throws, never allocates meaningfully.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.EngineVectorIndexFactory.Options
files.Summary: Backend options for every created index.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.EngineVectorIndexFactory
files.Summary: Own-engine factory: Flat → FlatExactIndex, Ivf → IvfFlatIndex, Hnsw → HnswIndex.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.FlatExactIndex.Options
files.Summary: Backend options: the ranking metric (default cosine).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.FlatExactIndex
files.Summary:
Own-engine exact backend: SIMD brute-force scan (Vector512→256→128, scalar fallback)
over the in-memory float[] store. Fully built in memory; Flush is a no-op.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswBeamSearcher
files.Summary:
Exact analog of the canonical HNSW SEARCH-LAYER routine, in score form (higher = closer):
candidate heap = max-heap by score (top = nearest candidate, expanded first), result heap
= min-heap by score bounded to ef (top = worst kept result = the stop gate). A candidate
whose score falls below the gate stops the beam. The visited set resets per layer
traversal (canonical: fresh visited per searchLayer call); the query score cache lives in
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswSearchContext" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and persists across layers of the same query. Returns
results sorted best-first (score desc, node id asc).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswBuilder
files.Summary:
Own HNSW construction (canonical INSERT algorithm, level-0 full beam): inserts each item
in order, greedily descends from the entry point through layers above the node's top
level, then beam-inserts per layer with the M / maxM neighbor pruning heuristic
(keep-if-closer-than-direct-neighbors). Writes backlinks for pruned victims.
Deterministic: seeded level assignment + insertion order + deterministic tie-breaks.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswCandidate
files.Summary: A single candidate during graph traversal: node id + metric score.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswGraph
files.Summary:
Immutable-after-build layered HNSW graph topology: per-node adjacency sets per layer,
plus the entry node and current max level. Pure data: ids/vectors live in
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorItemStore" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>; the graph only stores link structure (int ids). Mutations
happen only during construction — the finished graph is published in one reference swap
and never modified afterwards (immutable-index semantics, ARCHITECTURE.md addendum).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswIndex
files.Summary:
Own-engine HNSW backend with IMMUTABLE-INDEX + BATCH-REBUILD semantics (patent-avoidance
design, ARCHITECTURE.md addendum 2026-10-13): the layered graph is fully rebuilt from the
item store on every Build, Add, and Remove — there is deliberately NO incremental update
of a live graph, the method covered by US 15/929,802 "Dynamic Updates for HNSW". Core
construction + layered greedy/beam search (unpatented) is implemented from scratch.
Mutations mark the published graph dirty; the next search rebuilds it once (same
batch-rebuild behavior as <xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.IvfFlatIndex" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>). Cosine metric: vectors are
L2-normalized internally. Deterministic given the same items in the same order + seed.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswLevelAssigner
files.Summary:
Deterministic level assignment for HNSW layers: each node's top level is drawn from the
geometric distribution ⌊-ln(U)/ln(levelFactor)⌋ (U uniform in [0,1), factor < 1). Own
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.SeededRandom" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> keeps level assignment stable across .NET versions/platforms; same
seed + same insertion order → identical layer structure.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswOptions
files.Summary:
HNSW backend tuning parameters, mirroring the canonical algorithm's knobs:
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswOptions.M" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> outgoing links per node above layer 0 (<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswOptions.MaxLevel0Connections" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
on layer 0, typically 2·M), <xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswOptions.LevelFactor" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> as the level-assignment divisor
(1/ln(M) canonically), <xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswOptions.EfConstruction" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> beam width while inserting,
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswOptions.EfSearch" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> beam width at query time, and the deterministic
<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswOptions.Seed" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> for level assignment. Same seed + same insertion order → same graph.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswPublishedGraph
files.Summary:
The published immutable snapshot of a built HNSW graph: row-order ids parallel to the
normalized vector rows and the graph topology. Swapped in atomically after each full
rebuild; never mutated afterwards (batch-rebuild semantics).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswSearchContext
files.Summary:
Reusable traversal context for one built HNSW graph: row-order ids parallel to
normalized vector rows, a per-query dot-product score cache (NaN = unscored; zero-vector
queries legitimately score 0 and MUST be rescored), and the visited set shared by
construction-time multi-layer traversals. Score cache + visited set are reset per query
(<xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswSearchContext.ResetForNewQuery" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>); the query is copied into a reusable buffer so no span
state is held across calls.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.HnswSearcher
files.Summary:
Query-time traversal over a built HNSW graph: greedy descent from the entry point
through upper layers to layer 1, then a single ef-bounded beam search on layer 0,
sorted best-first. Read-only over the published immutable graph.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.IvfFlatIndex.Options
files.Summary: Backend options: metric, cluster count, probe count, k-means effort, deterministic seed.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.IvfFlatIndex
files.Summary:
Own-engine IVF-Flat: deterministic k-means coarse quantizer + inverted lists;
search probes the nprobe nearest clusters (by quantizer metric) and scores members
exactly. Mutations mark the partition stale; the next search rebuilds it (batch-rebuild
semantics per the 2026-10-13 addendum). Flush is a no-op (in-memory).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.FlatJsonVectorIndex
files.Summary:
Default zero-dependency backend over the JSON namespace-file format:
brute-force cosine (dot product over L2-normalized vectors), transactional flush.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.DefaultGpuContextPolicy
files.Summary:
Default policy: GPU-first discovery (CUDA/OpenCL per options), optional CPU fallback
acceptance (off by default — availability must reflect real GPUs only). Device
selection prefers CUDA > OpenCL and never throws when none exist.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuAccelerator
files.Summary:
Owns the ILGPU Context and the resolved accelerator. The GPU hand-shake runs once,
lazily, on first access, inside a lock, and every failure mode (builder exception,
missing driver, no acceptable device, accelerator-creation failure) collapses to
IsAvailable=false. Nothing here throws for 'no GPU present'.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuDiscoveryOptions
files.Summary:
How the ILGPU context is built for accelerator discovery. GPU-first builders enable
CUDA/OpenCL discovery; the flag set mirrors what the host considers acceptable.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuDistanceMetric
files.Summary: Backend metric shared with the engine kernels (mirrors VectorDistanceMetric).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuFlatIndex.Options
files.Summary: Backend options: ranking metric (default cosine) + launch chunking.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuFlatIndex
files.Summary:
GPU-accelerated exact flat index (ILGPU kernel scan). When no GPU is available the
injected CPU fallback IVectorIndex is used for every operation with identical
semantics — the fallback path must pass the engine conformance suite unchanged.
Kernels load lazily; all GPU faults collapse to CPU-fallback execution.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuIvfIndex.Options
files.Summary: Backend options: mirrors the engine IVF options + ranking metric + launch chunking.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuIvfIndex
files.Summary:
GPU-accelerated IVF index: the deterministic engine k-means partitions the corpus
(CPU-side, same algorithm as IvfFlatIndex so partitions are identical), GPU kernels
score (1) coarse centroids and (2) in-cluster members. When no GPU is available the
injected CPU fallback IVectorIndex is used with identical semantics.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuLaunchOptions
files.Summary:
Kernel-launch policy: rows per launch chunk and the per-launch thread cap. Chunked
launches keep the per-thread flat loop short and bounded on every backend (including
ILGPU's CPU simulator, which materializes one thread per index).

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuMetricCodec
files.Summary: Mapping from the engine metric enum onto the GPU kernel's int metric code.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuVectorIndexFactory
files.Summary:
Factory that produces <xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuFlatIndex" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> for <xref href="ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IndexKind.Gpu" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and
delegates every other kind to the injected CPU <xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorIndexFactory" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>. The
GPU index receives the standard <xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.IGpuAccelerator" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> availability gate and
wraps a flat CPU fallback <xref href="ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorIndex" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> as its transparent CPU fallback,
so search semantics are identical whether or not an accelerator is present.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuVectorKernels
files.Summary:
ILGPU kernels: one thread per score slot, plain loops, no barriers/shared memory —
identical accumulation order on every backend (CPU simulator included), so GPU and
fallback results are bit-for-bit reproducible for the same inputs.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.GpuVectorMatrix
files.Summary:
GPU-resident row-major vector matrix with lazy (re)upload: CPU-side rows + norms are
mirrored to device buffers; uploads overwrite exactly the changed range. Ownership
and synchronization live here — indexes never touch ILGPU buffers directly.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.IGpuAccelerator
files.Summary:
Availability handle for the ILGPU runtime: owns the Context and exposes the resolved
accelerator lazily. Construction never throws and never touches GPU drivers; every
member is guarded so machines without CUDA/OpenCL observe IsAvailable=false.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.IGpuContextPolicy
files.Summary:
ILGPU accelerator hand-shake: a GPU-first context (CUDA + OpenCL as configured) with
device classes the caller considers acceptable. All discovery is exception-
guarded; a machine without GPU drivers simply observes IsAvailable=false.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.IGpuScoreLauncher
files.Summary:
Compiled-kernel launcher boundary: hides ILGPU's launcher delegates behind an
injectable abstraction so index classes stay backend-agnostic and testable.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.IlgpuScoreLauncher
files.Summary:
Lazy, guarded ILGPU kernel launcher: kernels compile on first launch only (never at
construction), launches are chunked per GpuLaunchOptions, and every launch ends with
a synchronize so scored results are deterministically visible on the host.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorEmbedder
files.Summary: The host-injected embedding seam. The library never bundles, downloads, or selects embedding models — it consumes vectors from whatever the host wires in, and it validates them instead: and are recorded with every vector namespace, and any index whose hash or dimension mismatches the embedder is rejected rather than silently mixing embeddings from different models.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorIndex
files.Summary:
The pluggable dense-vector index contract. The library ships four backends, all interchangeable through this interface (they pass one shared conformance suite): IndexKind.FlatJson (zero-dependency JSON file, brute-force cosine), IndexKind.Flat (in-memory exact search with SIMD kernels), IndexKind.Ivf (k-means inverted lists for corpus sizes where full scans get expensive), and IndexKind.Hnsw (navigable-small-world graph; built with immutable/rebuild semantics and searched with a layered greedy beam). A GPU tier (ILGPU, transparent CPU fallback) wraps any of these for machines with devices.

Vector contract: vectors are L2-normalized at index time; scores are cosine similarities (higher = closer, 1.0 = identical). is fixed at construction; every item/query with a different dimension is rejected. Concurrency: implementations own their internal synchronization; concurrent Add/Remove/Search from multiple threads is safe.

Backends compare sets, not orderings: ranking parity between backends is exact for Flat/FlatJson and statistically guaranteed (recall ≥0.95 on the fixture) for the ANN tiers — results are ranked identically after fusion because ordering derives from scores, not insertion sequence.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorIndexFactory
files.Summary: Creates vector indexes of a requested for one dimension. Implementations decide concrete wiring (metrics, seeds, backing storage); the factory keeps index creation out of retrieval code so backends stay swappable by configuration alone. The default EngineVectorIndexFactory produces the own-engine backends; the GPU factory decorates a CPU fallback with ILGPU kernels.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorIndexGuard
files.Summary: Guards model hash + vector dimension at every index mutation boundary.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IvfMember
files.Summary: One IVF member: id, vector, assigned cluster.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IvfPostingLists
files.Summary: Inverted lists: cluster id → member rows + centroid access for probing.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.KMeansQuantizer
files.Summary:
OWN deterministic k-means (Lloyd iterations, seeded) — the IVF coarse quantizer.
Deterministic given the same training rows: seeded Fisher-Yates seeding, squared-L2
assignment via the SIMD scanner, mean update, empty clusters reseated on the globally
farthest points (deterministic order). Internally uses squared L2 regardless of the
search metric — IVF coarse assignment is metric-agnostic partitioning.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.KMeansResult
files.Summary: Result of one k-means run: centroids plus label arrays over the training rows.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.ScalarVectorOps
files.Summary:
In-package scalar math for the FlatJson backend (instance-based, no static state).
Deliberately separate from the Engine package's SIMD VectorMath: the base package must
stay dependency-free below itself, and cosine/normalize here are O(dim) scalar loops —
the flat JSON backend's cost is dominated by I/O, not arithmetic.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.ScoredVectorId
files.Summary: Vector index search hit.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.SeededRandom
files.Summary:
Pure deterministic pseudo-random generator (xorshift64*) used wherever the engine needs
seeded randomness (level assignment, quantizer seeding). Own implementation instead of
<xref href="System.Random" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> so results are stable across .NET versions and platforms.
Thread-unsafe by design: engine components own dedicated instances.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorDistanceMetric
files.Summary: Distance metric for vector-to-vector comparisons inside the engine.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorIndexGuard
files.Summary: Guard record binding a vector namespace to an embedder model hash/dim.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorIndexGuardMismatchException
files.Summary: Embedder model hash or vector dimension does not match the index guard.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorIndexIdNotFoundException
files.Summary: Remove of an id that is not present in the index.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorItem
files.Summary: A vector index item: id + vector.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorItemStore
files.Summary:
Mutable in-memory store shared by engine indexes: ids in row order parallel to vector
rows plus id → row map. Owns synchronization; build/add/remove/dim-guard semantics.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorMath
files.Summary:
PURE STATIC UTILITY (no mutable state, thread-safe by construction; the one sanctioned
static exception per architecture principles). Stateless numeric kernels for the engine:
dot product via Vector512 → Vector256 → Vector128 with scalar fallback, norm, normalize,
cosine. Deterministic order of accumulation for a given hardware width.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorNamespaceFile.Content
files.Summary: Content of one namespace file: guard + entries.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorNamespaceFile.Entry
files.Summary: Sets are keyed by id; a re-set id replaces the entry.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorNamespaceFile
files.Summary:
On-disk JSON vector index file format (one file per scope/model-hash namespace):
temp-file + atomic swap on write; open enforces the model-hash/dim guard.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorScanner
files.Summary: Scans rows with the metric's SIMD kernel; shared scoring core for flat/IVF search.

files.Title: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.VectorTopKBuffer
files.Summary: Bounded top-k min-heap buffer over (id, score); scores rise to the top.
